result.rationale:
Rhythm of the lap: a commit-and-brake opening, then the crest and drop through the Cathedral, then the back-straight slipstream, then the hairpin and switchback, then a climb to an opening final corner that slingshots you into T1. Speeds below come from a point-mass estimate (1.3 g cornering, 1.2 g braking, 230 km/h cap).

1. Main straight (0-380 m from the line; with the 220 m grid straight, 600 m of straight in all). 14 m wide, gently downhill at -1.6%. Asphalt aprons both sides, with a pit wall on the right and a spectator fence on the left. Top speed about 218 km/h.

2. T1 Sawmill: right, R42, 100 degrees, 83 km/h.
- Heavy braking downhill after the longest run, so lockups and late lunges happen here.
- The road is 14 m wide so two cars fit side by side.
- Gravel (14 to 26 m) with tyres outside, continuing along the 70 m Sawmill exit.
- Apex kerb on the inside, exit kerb on the outside.

3. Resin esses: left then right, both R120 and 55 degrees, about 140 km/h, climbing at 2.6-3%.
- A quick flick you can take flat with a clean line.
- Grass run-off, an apex kerb on the inside of each half and an exit kerb on the outside.

4. Lookout climb (120 m at +4.2%) and Lookout crest: a flat left kink, R300 and 20 degrees, at the highest point (22.5 m). It is blind, at about 190 km/h.

5. The Plunge: 60 m at -6.7%. The bank starts building here.

6. The Cathedral: the signature corner, described below.
- Entry: R170 tightening to 95 over 60 degrees.
- Exit: R95 tightening to 65 over 55 degrees.
- About 200 m long in all, downhill, banked from 0.05 up to 0.08 rad and back to 0.05.
- Speed falls from about 167 to 104 km/h.
- Grass outside the entry, gravel (20 to 26 m) with tyres outside the exit, kerbs on the apex and exit.

7. Back straight: 661 m of straight in two parts, both 13 m wide.
- Part one drops to a creek bridge at the lowest point (1 m).
- Part two, the Creek rise, climbs gently into the braking zone. Braking uphill shortens stopping distances and forgives late lunges.
- About 215 km/h at the end.

8. Creek hairpin: right, R30, 160 degrees, 70 km/h, 14 m wide.
- The tightest corner on the lap, with deep gravel (22 to 28 m) and tyres outside.
- The hairpin opens out at 20 degrees to the back straight, so the two legs never come within 132 m of each other.

9. Kingfisher drag: 280 m, climbing, with exit gravel and an exit kerb on the outside.

10. Twin Pines: a double-apex left, at about 100 then 91 km/h.
- First apex R60 over 70 degrees, then a 90 m link, then R50 over 80 degrees.
- Gravel outside both apexes, apex kerbs inside.
- Its direction is the opposite of the hairpin's, which creates the switchback.

11. Ridge road and Ridge brow: 380 m in total, climbing 8.5 m to a crest, then slightly downhill into the next braking zone. This gives the climb from the creek a payoff.

12. Lantern: right, opening from R55 to R150 over 155 degrees, 95 to 151 km/h.
- Late braking on entry over gravel (18 to 12 m) with tyres. The opening radius rewards committing early to the throttle.
- Its exit speed carries down the grid straight into the T1 slipstream, so a good Lantern sets up the next lap's first overtake.

13. Grid straight: 220 m with asphalt aprons, and the 4-car grid sits on it. The bank fades to 0 before the line.

Why it suits a phone-steered party racer:
- Every corner is separated by a straight, with no chain of tight technical corners.
- Only two corners are under 45 m radius: the hairpin (R30) and T1 (R42).
- Bank is continuous across every segment join, so the generator's 20 m smoothing never has to hide a step.
- Road width changes by at most 1 m between segments: 14 m at the grid, T1 and the hairpin; 12-13 m elsewhere.
- Kerbs are 1.2 m wide and 0.04-0.06 m high, kept flat on exits for touch drivers.
- The steepest segment grade is 6.7% (the Plunge). The sharpest crest change is about 9.6%, which the generator's 416 m crest-radius limit turns into a light, unloading crest rather than a jump.

Lap time:
- About 1:26 at the limit and 1:34 at a softer "party pace" (1.05 g, 216 km/h).
- That is quicker than the 1:40-2:00 target. My guess is that touch steering, assists and traffic will put real laps near 1:40, but that has not been tested.
- If it needs to be slower, tighten the Lantern entry to R48 and Twin Pines two to R45, and add 50-80 m to the Kingfisher drag. These keep the character of the lap.
result.signatureCorner:
The Lookout-Cathedral combination: the drop and the sweeper under the pines.
- You crest the circuit's highest point blind at about 190 km/h through a flat left kink.
- The road then falls away down the Plunge (-6.7%) and bends right into the Cathedral.
- The Cathedral is a downhill, banked right of about 200 m, tightening from R170 to R65 over 115 degrees, lined with tall pines.
- The brave carry speed in on the banking, but the tightening radius forces a trail-brake while still turning downhill.
- It allows two lines: committing early and wide, or braking early and taking a tight late apex.
- It also feeds the longest straight on the lap (661 m), so exit speed decides the slipstream fight to the hairpin. People will talk about "lifting at the Lookout".
Secondary feature: the opening-radius Lantern, which slingshots cars into the T1 slipstream.
result.overtakingZones:
1. Creek hairpin, the main zone.
- The 661 m back straight gives a full slipstream run at about 215 km/h.
- Braking is uphill from 215 to 70 km/h in a 14 m wide braking zone, which is easy to judge and forgives a late lunge.
- Deep gravel outside punishes anyone who overcooks it.

2. T1 Sawmill.
- 600 m of straight (380 m from the line, plus the grid) with a slipstream from the opening Lantern.
- Heavy downhill braking from about 218 to 83 km/h in a 14 m wide braking zone. This is the classic first-lap and last-lap move.

3. Twin Pines one: the switchback, or cutback.
- Twin Pines turns left, the opposite way to the right-hand hairpin.
- A driver who dives inside at the hairpin is left on the wrong side and gets a compromised exit.
- The defender can cross over, get the better drive up the 280 m Kingfisher drag, and re-pass on the inside into Twin Pines.

Bonus: Lantern, after the 380 m Ridge road with braking over the brow. It is a fourth, lower-percentage chance, and it decides who leads into the T1 slipstream.

result.rationale:
Summary: clockwise, 44 segments, startZ 0. Road width 12-14 m. Elevation runs from -13 to +9.5 m relative to the start line; trackgen expects the start at 0, so the layout uses that. The only corner tighter than 45 m is the hairpin (R30). Every corner has spiral entries and exits. Corners carry mild camber that follows curvature (up to 0.06 rad), with the outside edge higher.

Corner by corner:

1. Main straight and grid (220 m before the line + 280 m after, 14 m wide, near flat).
- The 4-car grid sits on the 220 m before the line.
- Paved aprons and a pit wall appear only here (plus the asphalt run-off on the left at the Last Pines exit).
- About 500 m of slipstream into T1.

2. T1 Gatehouse: R48, 105 deg right.
- Spiral entry 28 deg, 50 deg at R48, exit 27 deg. Road 13.5 m.
- Heavy braking on level ground, from top speed to about 108 km/h.
- Gravel trap 20-28 m with tyres on the outside, apex kerb inside, exit kerb backed by gravel.

3. Bracken drop: 80 m at -6%, the steepest grade on the lap. It plunges to the valley floor.

4. Fernbrook kink: 16 deg left, R260, pure spirals.
- Flat out over the brook at the low point (compression).
- Kerbs on the apex and the exit.

5. Pinewood Esses: right-left-right (34/58/34 deg at R125/112/125) on a steady 3% climb through the trees.
- A gentle 2.5 m gap between each pair of corners.
- About 150-175 km/h: the brave stay flat, everyone else lifts. Smooth drag inputs, not technical.
- Inside kerbs on every apex and outside kerbs on every exit; grass run-off.

6. Hilltop: R90, 71 deg right, uphill onto the ridge (about 148 km/h). Grass 18 m.

7. The crest: 110 m at +4.1% to a blind brow (the high point, +9.5 m), then a 276 m run downhill (-2.2%). The Cathedral opens up below you.

8. The Cathedral: a 145 deg downhill double-apex right (see signature corner).

9. Back straight: 430 m, running diagonally north-east through the valley.
- Dips to the lowest point (-13 m), then rises +1.7% in the last 120 m. Braking uphill gives stable, late braking.

10. Kingfisher hairpin: R30, 140 deg left (spirals 26/30 deg). Road 13.5-14 m.
- About 86 km/h, the slowest point on the lap.
- 24-30 m gravel trap with tyres on the outside (right).
- It turns against the circuit's direction, which breaks up the rhythm.

11. Owl rise: 150 m at +2.6%, climbing west out of the hairpin.

12. Lookout: R110, 90 deg uphill right (about 163 km/h), then the Lookout brow (+4%, a small blind rise) and a short drop.

13. Last Pines: R80, 95 deg right (about 139 km/h) onto the main straight.
- A good exit sets up the slipstream fight into T1.

Run-off and kerbs:
- Gravel with tyre walls only outside the slow corners (T1, Cathedral, Kingfisher). Grass with armco everywhere else.
- Kerbs on apexes and exits. Run-off 6-30 m.
- No-kerb sides have kerbHeight 0, because trackgen adds kerbHeight at the asphalt edge even when kerbWidth is 0.

Separation: legs more than 500 m apart along the lap stay at least 208 m apart. No two legs come close to touching.

Lap time:
- The M8 racing-line model (vMax 51 m/s, lateral 15 m/s², braking 11 m/s²) puts an ideal lap at about 1:15 on a relaxed line and 1:21 on the centre line.
- I expect casual touch-steer players to be about 20-30% slower, roughly 1:35-1:45, inside the 1:40-2:00 target. This is an estimate, not a measurement.
- Getting a 1:40 ideal lap on 3.3 km would need a stop-start layout, which goes against the brief.

Different from g-track-2, and better for this game:
- g-track-2 runs counter-clockwise: a trapezoid with a long diagonal on the right and a hairpin at the bottom right. Owlwood is clockwise, shaped like a "7", with the hairpin pointing inward and an inside-diagonal back straight.
- It has 3 heavy-braking zones (the checker lists all three) where g-track-2 has 1-2.
- It adds a named signature corner, a blind crest and a downhill plunge.

Shape check (turning-function distance, lower is more alike):
- g-track-2: 0.63. For scale, g-track-2 vs the Speed Dreams 'forza' track is 0.44, and the median between unrelated Speed Dreams tracks is 0.97.
- The closest Speed Dreams track is ruudskogen (a model of Rudskogen) at 0.58. Only the one-hairpin rhythm in the curvature profile drives that match. The two are clearly different on the side-by-side render (compare.png).
- I checked by eye against the real circuits on the forbidden list and saw no match.

For trackgen closure in overrides: use straights ['crest run','Lookout run'] (headings about 96 deg apart) and arc 'Last Pines'.
result.signatureCorner:
The Cathedral is a 145 deg downhill double-apex right of about 200 m, in the far south-west corner under the tallest pines.

How it is built:
- Spiral entry 20 deg into apex 1: R68 for 40 deg.
- The 'nave' opens to R120 for 12 deg.
- It then tightens into apex 2: R52 for 33 deg, followed by a 20 deg exit spiral.
- The road is 12.5 m wide and drops 8.5 m (about 5%) through the corner.
- Camber builds to 0.06 rad at the second apex.

How it plays: you arrive over the blind crest and brake downhill from about 180 km/h. The first apex is quick (about 129 km/h). Because the second apex is tighter (about 116 km/h), carrying too much speed through the nave sends you wide into the gravel. The corner rewards patience and a late second apex, and leads onto the longest straight.

Run-off: gravel with tyre walls 18-26 m on the outside (left), kerbs on both apexes, and an exit kerb backed by gravel.

It allows two lines, so players can race side by side or cut back under at the second apex.
result.overtakingZones:
1. Main straight into T1 Gatehouse (best). There are 500 m of slipstream: the 220 m grid straight, the line, then 280 m. Braking is heavy and level, from about 184 to 108 km/h, into a 13.5 m wide R48 right. The gravel outside forgives an overcooked dive.

2. Diagonal back straight into the Kingfisher hairpin (the heaviest stop). The back straight is 430 m, plus the Cathedral exit. Braking is uphill, from top speed to about 86 km/h, into a 14 m wide R30 left. It is a classic outbraking spot with a deep gravel trap. A good exit from the Cathedral decides it.

3. Crest run into the Cathedral. There are 386 m of straight over the blind brow, then downhill braking (about 184 to 129 km/h) into apex 1. Racers can outbrake into the entry, or take the second, tighter apex on the switchback.

Bonus: a strong exit from Last Pines (about 139 km/h) sets up zone 1 on the next lap.

result.rationale:
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM CANDIDATES A AND B: Timberfall (a) and Owlwood (b) both run clockwise. Both have the main straight on the north edge and a right-hand T1 of radius 42-48 m. Kettle Hollow runs counter-clockwise. Its main straight is on the south edge, T1 is a tighter left, and a carousel sits at the end of a tongue that pokes out of the northwest corner. On the map it looks like a kettle with a spout. The lap has 11 turns, only one under 45 m, and never more than two technical corners in a row.

CORNER BY CORNER (counter-clockwise, start at 34 m elevation):
- Main straight: 170 m after the line plus 250 m behind it, 420 m in total, 14 m wide. Paved aprons, with the pit wall on the infield side. It climbs from Campfire to the line, and the grid sits on the nearly flat last 120 m. It then drops 2 m to T1.
- T1 Hatchet: 105 deg left, radius 30 m with spiral entry and exit, 14 m wide. You brake downhill from about 205 to 70 km/h. Gravel trap 24-30 m deep with tyres behind, apex kerb and exit kerb. It is the lap-1 chaos corner: square enough to dive up the inside, wide enough for two cars side by side.
- Hatchet rise: 115 m straight at +2%.
- T2/T3 Lynx dogleg: 50 deg right (R 130), a 90 m run, then 50 deg left (R 110), climbing. Fast and flowing at about 140/130 km/h with a light lift. Easy on drag steering.
- Pine run: 120 m straight.
- T4 Timberline: 80 deg uphill left (R 85) onto the ridge, about 115 km/h. A corner you commit to, and its exit sets your speed for the longest flat-out stretch of the lap.
- Timberline crest: 90 m straight at the highest point, 50 m.
- T5/T6 Ranger's flick: 18 deg right then 18 deg left (R 300) just over the brow. Nearly flat out at 175-200 km/h. A thrill, and the place you pick your slipstream line.
- The Firebreak and the Plunge: 296 m at -1.7%, then 150 m at -7%. 446 m of unbroken straight at about 230 km/h, and the Kettle bowl opens up below you.
- T7 THE KETTLE: signature corner (details below).
- Kettle climb: 200 m at +6.25%, running parallel to the Firebreak and 114 m from it. Through the trees you see the cars still coming down.
- T8 Badger's Drop: 120 deg right (R 50). You brake uphill, where stops are short and stable, the apex is on a blind crest, and then the road falls away (22 m at -7.3%). Gravel on the outside.
- T9 Badger's tail: 60 deg left (R 75) at the bottom, about 108 km/h. With T8 it forms a corkscrew-style right-left that drops about 7 m.
- T10 Splinters: 36 deg downhill right (R 170) at about 150 km/h. Flat out if you hit the apex.
- The chute: 120 m straight.
- T11 Campfire: 91 deg left (R 70) at about 105 km/h. Gravel outside and a paved exit apron. Your exit speed decides the drag race to the line.

ELEVATION AND RULES: elevation runs 24-50 m (26 m range). The steepest segment averages 7.27%. Road width is 12-14 m, run-off 8-30 m. Gravel is on the outside of T1, T7, T8, T9 and T11, grass everywhere else, and asphalt only on the main straight and the Campfire exit. Kerbs are on every apex and exit, and banking stays within +-0.12 rad. Barriers line the whole lap, so there are no shortcuts. Every sharp corner has gravel or wide grass run-off.

LAP TIME: my point-mass estimate is 1:20 with a grippy car (1.15 g) and 1:30 with a softer one (0.9 g, 170 W/kg, top speed about 213 km/h). Candidates a and b come out at 1:25/1:36 and 1:21/1:31 on the same two models. So all three are probably faster than the 1:40-2:00 target unless the game's grip is lower. If the lap needs to be slower, tightening T4 or T11 is the simplest fix.
result.signatureCorner: T7 THE KETTLE: a 180 deg downhill left carousel around a glacial kettle hole at the end of the forest tongue. Constant radius 55 m with 26 deg spiral entry and exit, banked 0.12 rad (the maximum allowed), 13.5 m wide. It drops 4 m through the bowl to the lowest point of the lap (24 m). You arrive at about 230 km/h off the 7% Plunge, brake hard (about 140 m), and the banking catches you. You hold about 100 km/h around the bowl for 5-6 seconds, get squeezed at the bottom, and climb straight out. The banking lets two cars run side by side, with an inside line and an outside line that cuts back on the exit. The return leg runs 114 m away from the approach, so you can see rivals through the trees. A second talking point is T8-T9 Badger's Drop, a corkscrew-style right turn over a blind crest that drops 7% and flicks left.
result.overtakingZones:
OT1: main straight (420 m from Campfire, 170 m from the line) into T1 Hatchet. About 205 to 70 km/h over 120 m of downhill braking, 14 m wide. This is the 4-car start pile-up, and late brakers can dive up the inside.
OT2 (the main one): Firebreak plus Plunge (446 m of straight after the nearly flat Ranger's flick, about 820 m flat out from Timberline) into T7 the Kettle. About 230 to 100 km/h over 140 m, with the best slipstream on the lap. The banking allows inside and outside lines and a cut-back on the exit.
OT3: Kettle climb (200 m uphill out of the slow Kettle exit, so cars bunch up and slipstream) into T8 Badger's Drop. About 180 to 90 km/h over 80 m. Uphill braking is short and stable, which suits touch controls. Dive before the crest.
Bonus late-lap lunge: the chute into T11 Campfire, about 190 to 105 km/h, with gravel outside.

- A trapezoid base.
- Two parallel forest legs about 180 m apart.
- A ridge arm bending NW at the top.
- A 205-degree descending spiral lobe hanging off the end of that arm.

I threw away an earlier "sock" draft because its triangle-with-balloon silhouette was too close to Speed Dreams g-track-1. The final shape has no long diagonal, and it doesn't resemble g-track-2 or any real circuit I know of.

The lap runs counter-clockwise: 9 corners, 3313 m, elevation 5.9 to 33.9 m.

LAP-TIME MODEL: I added a point-mass lap model to the tooling (1.0 g cornering, 0.97 g braking, 230 km/h top speed, grade-aware). It gives an 89.1 s ideal lap, which is about 1:42 with a typical 15% human/phone margin, inside the 1:40-2:00 target. Top speed is about 204 km/h.

1. Main straight (s 0-280, 14 m wide). The start line sits on a gentle brow at 16 m. The grid straight (210 m, 4 slots) climbs to the line; the main straight then falls 3.5 m toward the brook. There are paved aprons here only, with the pit wall on the infield and a catch-fenced spectator side outside.

2. T1 Millrace (120-degree left, R42 with spirals, 13 m wide, s 280-386). The first heavy stop, from about 198 to 74 km/h, slightly downhill. Gravel and tyres outside, kerbs inside on the late entry, apex and exit, plus an outside exit kerb. The long 120-degree arc allows a cut-back on exit, and the gravel catches lap-1 lunges.

3. Brook run (130 m). A short squirt NW along the brook.

4. Sawpit (60-degree right, R90) and Woodcutter (30-degree left, R110), joined by a 60 m link: "the esses". One flowing right-left at the foot of the hill, about 108 then 119 km/h, taken with a lift and a dab. Grass runoff, kerbs on apexes and exits. It's a single S rather than a technical chain, so it stays phone-friendly.

5. The Ladder and Ladder top (260 m at a steady 6%). A hard climb from 17.6 to 33.5 m, reaching about 186 km/h.

6. The Brow (55-degree left, R180, s 1029-1237). A blind crest into a fast left: the road goes from +6% to slightly downhill right where you turn in. About 153 km/h minimum, so brave players barely lift. Wide 18-22 m grass runoff outside, because you can't see the exit.

7. Ridge straight (250 m at 32-34 m, the high plateau). Views across the forest: the Fernside valley falls away to the south-west, the main straight is visible far below, and the Kestrel spiral appears ahead. Top speed of about 204 km/h here.

8. Kestrel (205-degree left, s 1487-1822). This is the signature corner, described below. It drops 11.7 m with a 5.4% plunge, banked 0.06 into the turn. Gravel and tyres outside throughout, kerbs on the apex and exit.

9. Talon (25-degree right, R200, flat out). Unwinds the spiral and fires you out of the lobe.

10. Fernside (110 m), then Drop (55-degree right, R100, about 114 km/h). A medium-fast right that turns you south into the valley. Grass runoff.

11. Fernside descent (341 m), then Hollow drop (130 m). One 470 m downhill run, gentle at first, then steepening to -4.6% into the valley floor.

12. Hollow (70-degree right, R50, 13 m wide, banked 0.04). The compression at the bottom of the valley, at the lowest point of the lap (5.9 m). You brake downhill from about 204 to 80 km/h, and the car loads up through the dip at the apex before the road rises again. Gravel and tyres outside.

13. Back straight (311 m, 13 m wide). Rises gently out of the valley to about 176 km/h.

14. Switchback (160-degree left hairpin, R30, 13 m wide, banked 0.05). The uphill hairpin: it climbs about 4 m through the turn, and the uphill braking shortens stopping distances, which rewards a late dive. Gravel and tyres outside. Its exit decides the run up the grid and main straight to T1.

RHYTHM: brake, flow, climb, crest, spiral, dive, compression, hairpin, drag.

RULE CHECKS:
- Only two corners are under 45 m (T1 R42 and the Switchback R30).
- Every arc is at least 30 m radius.
- Width is 12-14 m.
- Bank stays within +/-0.06.
- Kerbs are 1.2 m wide and 0.04-0.06 m high.
- Runoff is 7-26 m.
result.signatureCorner:
THE KESTREL is a 205-degree descending, tightening left that winds about 12 m down around the summit knoll at the end of the ridge, like a helter-skelter.

How it unfolds:
- You see it coming. From the high Ridge straight you watch the road coil downhill ahead of you.
- Turn-in comes at about 188 km/h, with the radius opening at 400 m.
- The radius then shrinks steadily from 130 m to 55 m over 189 m of 5.4% downhill, banked into the turn.
- So you're trail-braking and adding steering all the way down, reaching about 84 km/h at the tightest point.
- It then opens at once (55 to 200 m) into the flat-out Talon right flick, which fires you toward the valley.

It's one long, readable steering input rather than a fiddly chain, which suits a touch-drag. It rewards commitment, because braking late at the entry and carrying speed down the spiral pays off all the way to the Drop. A big gravel trap and tyre wall sit on the outside, where the hillside falls away with views over the pines.

The lap leads into it with a supporting set-piece, the Brow: a blind crest at the top of a 6% climb into a fast R180 left.
result.overtakingZones:
1. MAIN STRAIGHT INTO T1 MILLRACE (primary)
- About 490 m flat-out, counting the grid and main straights from the Switchback exit.
- Ends at a slightly downhill stop from about 198 to 74 km/h into a 120-degree, R42 left.
- 13-14 m wide, with gravel outside.
- The long arc allows a switch-back on exit.

2. FERNSIDE DESCENT INTO THE HOLLOW
- A 470 m downhill straight that steepens to -4.6%.
- Ends with braking from about 204 to 80 km/h into the R50 right at the valley-floor compression, 13 m wide.
- Downhill braking makes stopping distances longer and less certain, so a brave late-braker can steal the inside before the dip.

3. BACK STRAIGHT INTO THE SWITCHBACK
- A 311 m gently rising straight (about 176 km/h) into the R30 uphill hairpin, 13 m wide.
- Uphill braking shortens stopping distances, inviting a late dive up the inside.
- A better hairpin exit then sets up a second slipstream pass into T1, so zones 3 and 1 chain together.

BONUS (for the brave): the 250 m Ridge straight into the Kestrel entry, where cars brake from about 188 to 130 km/h. A pass here is possible but risky on a descending, tightening corner.

scores.name: Kestrel Ridge (d)
scores.bestIdeas:
- The lap tells one simple story over one hill: a hard left at T1, the 6% Ladder climb, the blind Brow, the Ridge straight along the top, the Kestrel spiralling down, the 470 m Fernside dive, the Hollow dip at the valley floor, then the uphill Switchback hairpin and the drag to the line. The elevation profile is easy to remember, and its 28 m range is the biggest of the four.
- Signature corner: the Kestrel, a 205-degree left that tightens as it spirals downhill around a knoll. Because you can see it coiling below you from the Ridge straight, it is readable before you get there. It is the most visually distinctive corner in the set, and the one people will talk about.
- The "?" hook outline is unique. It makes a memorable minimap shape and is not like any Speed Dreams track: against my re-run of the turning-function test, forza is closest at 0.59, g-track-2 is 0.65 and g-track-1 is 0.79, and side by side they look different.
- It is the only candidate where the checker finds all three intended overtaking zones as heavy braking zones: T1 Millrace, the Hollow and the Switchback. They also chain: pass at the uphill Switchback, then defend or re-pass into T1.
- Only 9 corners, with spiral entries and exits everywhere and just one esses pair. The two parallel legs of the neck are about 180 m apart, so you can see rivals through the trees.
scores.problems:
- The Kestrel tightens from R130 to R55 while dropping 5.4%. That means trail-braking and steering more and more at the same time, which is the hardest thing to do with a phone drag. I expect a lot of casual players to run wide on lap 1.
  - Suggested fix (from candidate C): tighten only to about R65-70, then hold a constant radius for the last 90 degrees with bank raised to 0.08-0.10, so the banking catches the car.
- The lap is too quick. Its 1:42 figure comes from its own softer model (1.0 g plus a 15% margin). On the shared racing-line model I re-ran on all four it is 1:21 on the centre line, the same as the others.
- The Brow is a blind crest straight into a left. On a quarter of a split-screen TV it needs chevrons or a marker board.
- The Hollow is braked downhill from about 204 km/h, so stopping distances are longer and less predictable for casual players. It needs generous gravel.
- The 470 m Fernside dive and the Ladder form a long, narrow neck that can feel like an out-and-back.
- The Sawpit and Woodcutter esses (about 108-119 km/h) are a little slow and fiddly for where they sit.
- Its longest straight is 470 m, which leaves less room for slipstream than A's 661 m.
- Mild risk: the sequence of the lap (a left T1, a long climb, a descending left onto a long downhill, a dip at the bottom, then a slow left onto the pit straight) echoes Mount Panorama. The outline is unrelated, but avoid leaning into that in names and dressing.
- Like g-track-2 it runs counter-clockwise with the start straight along the bottom. That resemblance is superficial.

scores.name: Timberfall Circuit (a)
scores.bestIdeas:
- The best racing package of the four. There are four real stops:
  - 600 m of straight into T1, braking downhill.
  - A 661 m slipstream run into an uphill R30 hairpin with a 14 m wide braking zone.
  - Twin Pines, which turns the opposite way to the hairpin, so a driver who dives inside at the hairpin can be re-passed on the cutback.
  - Lantern, the last corner.
- Lantern opens from R55 to R150 over 155 degrees: brake, turn in, then unwind and get on the throttle. It is very touch-friendly, and its exit carries down the grid straight into the T1 slipstream.
- Only 10 corners, each separated by a straight. It is the easiest track to learn in two laps.
- "Lift at the Lookout": a blind 190 km/h crest, then the -6.7% Plunge into a downhill, banked, tightening sweeper.
- On the shared racing-line model it is the slowest lap (1:24 on the centre line), so it is the closest to the 1:40-2:00 target.
scores.problems:
- No transition spirals on most corners. T1, the hairpin and Twin Pines go straight from a straight to R42, R30 and R50-60, so the corners look kinked and the racing line feels abrupt for sim-lite cars, unless the track generator smooths them.
- Of all the Speed Dreams tracks, its outline is most like "Corkscrew", the Speed Dreams model of Laguna Seca (turning-function distance 0.53, the lowest in the whole set). Side by side it looks clearly different, but a banned real circuit is the nearest match.
- It shares the Cathedral, Kingfisher and Lookout names with B. The signature idea (blind crest, plunge, tightening downhill sweeper) is also nearly the same as B's.
- The Cathedral tightens from R170 to R65 while going downhill, which is hard on a touch drag.
- The Twin Pines double left (R60, then a 90 m link, then R50) is the one slow, technical-ish stretch.
- Elevation range is 21.5 m and the scenery is fairly generic. There is no single shape you would remember from the minimap.
- The 661 m back straight is about 12 s with nothing to do, unless items or slipstream fill it.

scores.name: Kettle Hollow (c)
scores.bestIdeas:
- The Kettle is the most touch-friendly signature corner in the set: a 180-degree left of constant R55, banked at 0.12 rad, at the bottom of a 7% Plunge after about 820 m flat out. You hold one steady drag, the banking catches the car, there is room for an inside and an outside line, and the exit allows a cut-back. It is also instantly readable on a small split-screen view.
- The return leg runs 114 m from the approach, so you can watch rivals coming down through the trees. That is a great party moment.
- Ranger's flick: a pair of R300 kinks over the brow, nearly flat out. It is a cheap thrill and a place to pick your slipstream line.
- The "kettle with a spout" outline makes a memorable minimap shape.
- 26 m of elevation and a 50 m high point give strong views.
scores.problems:
- It is the candidate most like g-track-2:
  - It has the lowest g-track-2 score of the four (0.58), and g-track-2 is the closest Speed Dreams track to it.
  - Like g-track-2 it runs counter-clockwise, has a boxy body and has its start straight along the bottom. The brief specifically calls out g-track-2's "boxy shape with its start straight on the bottom".
- It is only 170 m from the line to an R30 T1, so lap 1 is a guaranteed pile-up for 4 cars. That is chaotic, but often frustrating rather than fun.
- The checker finds only one heavy braking zone.
- The third overtaking zone (the 200 m Kettle climb out of a 100 km/h corner) is weak.
- On the west side, T8 to T11 form a four-corner chain. Badger's Drop puts the apex on a blind crest, then drops 7% and flicks left, which is tricky with a phone drag.
- The Kettle's 0.12 rad bank and the 7.27% grade are both near the limits.
- "Carousel" and "corkscrew-style" both point at famous real corners.
- The lap is 1:20 on the shared model, too fast for the target.

scores.name: Owlwood Ring (b)
scores.bestIdeas:
- Clothoid spirals on every corner, so it is the smoothest geometry in the set.
- Separate parts of the track stay at least 208 m apart, which leaves deep forest between them and room for scenery.
- Practical trackgen notes from its write-up:
  - Set kerbHeight to 0 on sides with no kerb, because trackgen adds the kerb height at the asphalt edge even when the kerb width is 0.
  - Start at z = 0, which is what trackgen expects.
- The Fernbrook kink: a flat-out compression over the brook at the valley floor.
- Its tooling is worth reusing for any winner: a turning-function shape check against every Speed Dreams track, and a side-by-side render against g-track-2.
- The diagonal back straight cuts inward to the Kingfisher hairpin, which turns against the direction of the lap.
scores.problems:
- The east side is about 1.2 km of continuous gentle bending (T1, Bracken drop, the kink, the three-part esses, Hilltop), so there is a lot of steering and little punctuation. It feels busy on a phone drag, and there are few chances to brake late.
- The signature Cathedral is a double apex that tightens again after its middle section opens (R68, then R120, then R52). That is the hardest of the four signatures to read on a quarter of a TV.
- The west half (Lookout and Last Pines, two rounded right-handers of about 90 degrees) is a generic rounded rectangle.
- The longest straight is only 430 m.
- Its closest Speed Dreams track is ruudskogen (0.58), which models Rudskogen, a circuit on the banned list. It looks different side by side.
- It reuses the Cathedral, Kingfisher and Lookout names from A.
- It is the fastest lap (1:20.7 on the centre line), the furthest from the 1:40-2:00 target.

result.winner:
Kestrel Ridge (d). It wins on the lap's single-hill story, its unique "?" outline, the Kestrel spiral you can see coming from the ridge, and three overtaking zones the checker finds and that chain together. Before building it, graft in these ideas:
- From C: hold the bottom of the Kestrel at a constant radius with 0.08-0.10 rad bank, instead of tightening all the way to R55.
- From A: make the run into the Switchback 14 m wide and push it toward 400 m or more of slipstream. Make the Switchback exit open out like A's Lantern, so it slingshots onto the grid straight. Add chevrons at the Brow.
- From B: apply its practical trackgen notes (kerbHeight 0 on sides with no kerb, start at z = 0).
- Slow the lap toward the target by tightening one medium corner.

Timberfall (a) is a close second and the better pure racing track. Its weak points are corners with no transition spirals, an outline whose nearest Speed Dreams match is the Laguna Seca model, and a signature corner that is too like B's.

scores.name: Timberfall Circuit (candidate a)
scores.bestIdeas: 1) The best overtaking zone of the four: a 661 m back straight (creek bridge at the low point, then the Creek rise) into the R30 Creek hairpin. Braking is uphill and 14 m wide; my model has it at about 198 to 66 km/h over about 130 m. The checker counts 4 heavy-braking zones, the most of any candidate. 2) A switchback after the hairpin: the right-hand R30 hairpin, a 280 m drag, then the left-hand Twin Pines. A driver who dives at the hairpin can be cut back at Twin Pines, so passes can be answered. 3) The opening-radius final corner, Lantern (R55 opening to R150 over 155 degrees), rewards early throttle and slingshots cars down the grid straight into the T1 slipstream. 4) The Lookout crest (blind, about 190 km/h), then the Plunge, then the Cathedral, a downhill banked right tightening from R170 to R65: a good set-piece. 5) The slowest corners of the four put the party-pace lap at about 1:41.6 on my model (1.05 g / 216 km/h), the only candidate inside the 1:40-2:00 target. 6) Bank is continuous across every segment join, and width changes by at most 1 m.
scores.problems: 1) No spiral transitions anywhere. Every corner starts with a sudden step in curvature (straight straight into R30 or R42). The Resin esses flip from a left R120 to a right R120 with no link, which gives abrupt steering on touch-drag. 2) Very heavy on straights: about 68% of the lap (2.26 km of 3.3) is straight. The second half is stop-go: hairpin 66, Twin Pines 94 and 86, Lantern 90 km/h, all inside about 1 km. 3) Of the four, it has the lowest turning-function distance to any Speed Dreams track: Corkscrew (the Laguna Seca model) at 0.53. It looks nothing like it, but the long-straight/hairpin rhythm matches. 4) Only 60 m of Plunge separates the crest from turn-in, so the braking (about 181 to 98 km/h) happens inside a downhill corner that tightens, which makes the Cathedral entry harsh. 5) Kingfisher drag and the main straight carry camber on straight road. It is harmless but sloppy. 6) It shares the Cathedral, Kingfisher and Lookout names and its crest-sweeper-straight-hairpin sequence with candidate b.

scores.name: Owlwood Ring (candidate b)
scores.bestIdeas: 1) The most disciplined geometry: every corner has a spiral entry and exit, and the camber follows the curvature, so steering builds smoothly. That is ideal for touch-drag. 2) The widest forest buffer: legs stay at least 208 m apart. 3) Three clean braking zones: T1 Gatehouse after 500 m of slipstream (about 197 to 84 km/h, level ground), the Cathedral over a blind crest, and the Kingfisher hairpin after a 430 m diagonal (uphill braking, 14 m wide). 4) The Kingfisher hairpin turns left, against the circuit's clockwise direction, which breaks up the rhythm. 5) The Fernbrook kink, a flat-out compression over a brook at the low point, is cheap and memorable. 6) A useful trackgen note: put kerbHeight 0 on sides with no kerb, because trackgen raises the asphalt edge even when kerbWidth is 0. 7) Exit kerbs are backed by gravel on the slow corners.
scores.problems: 1) Built on the same template as candidate a: blind crest, downhill tightening right called 'Cathedral', longest straight, 'Kingfisher' hairpin, plus the Lookout name, so it has a weak identity of its own. 2) Its closest Speed Dreams shape is ruudskogen (a model of Rudskogen, which the brief explicitly forbids) at 0.58, then g-track-2 at 0.63. It looks different, but it is not as far from either as it should be. 3) The esses plus Hilltop make a 590 m chain of four direction changes (right, left, right, right). The esses angles are mild (34/58/34 degrees), so the section is long but bland. 4) The Cathedral's double apex (R68, opening to R120, then R52) braking downhill after a blind crest is too subtle for casual phone players, and passes there are a gamble. 5) The longest straight is only 430 m, the weakest slipstream of the four. 6) Last Pines (R80, about 105 km/h) and Hilltop have grass, not gravel, on the outside, and Last Pines has an asphalt exit run-off. 7) The lap is about 1:29 on my grippy model and 1:37.6 at party pace, below the 1:40 target.

scores.name: Kettle Hollow (candidate c)
scores.bestIdeas: 1) The Kettle: a 180-degree downhill carousel, R55, banked 0.12 rad. It is the most talked-about signature corner of the four. The banking supports inside and outside lines, so cars can run side by side, and it is a single long steady input, ideal for touch steering. 2) The longest flat-out stretch of the four: about 820 m from Timberline over the nearly flat Ranger's flick (R300, 18 degrees each way, over the brow) into the Kettle braking zone, at about 213 km/h. The flick is a cheap thrill to graft onto any long straight. 3) The Kettle climb runs 114 m from the approach, so drivers can see rivals through the trees. 4) The biggest scenic arc: Timberline crest at 50 m, the 7% Plunge with the bowl opening below, the lowest point in the kettle hole, and Badger's Drop over a blind crest. 5) Gravel is on the outside of every slow corner, with an asphalt apron only at the Campfire exit next to the start.
scores.problems: 1) T1 Hatchet (R30) is only 170 m after the line. The 4-car grid launches straight into a hairpin, so lap 1 is a guaranteed pile-up and there is no real drag race off the line. 2) It is the closest of the four to g-track-2: turning-function distance 0.58, its nearest match of all Speed Dreams tracks. Like g-track-2 it runs counter-clockwise, has its start straight on the bottom, and is a box with a hairpin lobe sticking out. It does not meet 'clearly different' comfortably. The 'corkscrew-style' T8-T9 also invites a Laguna Seca comparison. 3) A busy first sector: T1, T2, T3 and T4 all fall inside about 900 m with 90-120 m links, and T8, T9, T10 and T11 cluster again late in the lap. 4) The main braking zone is downhill at -7% into the carousel, a long and unstable stop, and the bank sits right at the 0.12 cap. 5) Badger's Drop puts a blind crest in the middle of an R50 corner, then drops 7.3%. That unloads the car while it is turning, which is hard on phone steering. 6) The steepest grades of the four: 7.27% max, the Kettle climb at 6.25% for 200 m, the Plunge at 7% for 150 m. 7) The fastest lap of the four (about 1:28 grippy, 1:36 party), so it is the furthest under target.

scores.name: Kestrel Ridge (candidate d)
scores.bestIdeas: 1) The most original silhouette: a tall hooked '?' with an outward lobe, not a rectangle with a notch. Its distance to g-track-2 is 0.65, and it looks like no Speed Dreams track or banned circuit. 2) The Kestrel: a 205-degree helter-skelter left that descends about 12 m at 5.4% while tightening from R130 to R55, then opens straight into the flat-out Talon flick. It is a genuinely new signature, readable from the Ridge straight before you reach it, and it rewards a late entry. 3) Three evenly spaced, clear overtaking zones, each after 311-490 m of straight: T1 Millrace (about 183 to 78 km/h), the Hollow compression at the bottom of the valley (about 193 to 86 km/h), and the uphill Switchback hairpin (about 165 to 66 km/h). The Switchback exit chains into the T1 slipstream for a second pass. 4) Only 9 corners, all with spiral entries and exits. The rhythm reads well (brake, flow, climb, blind brow, spiral, dive, compression, hairpin, drag), and there is never a technical chain. 5) The most elevation of the four (28 m): the 6% Ladder climb, the blind Brow at about 153 km/h with 22 m of grass run-off, and the Ridge plateau with views over the forest. 6) Gravel is on the outside of every slow corner and asphalt only at the start, kerbs are tidy, and bank and width are continuous across joins.
scores.problems: 1) About 2.1 km of the lap (63%) is 12 m wide: the Ladder, the Ridge, the Kestrel and Fernside. That is legal, but it is the narrow end for 4 cars side by side, and the Kestrel's claim of two lines needs 13-13.5 m. 2) The Kestrel is about 270 m of trail-braking down a slope while the radius tightens, with only 0.06 rad of bank. That is demanding on a phone, and dive attempts there will mostly end in the gravel. 3) Braking into the Hollow is downhill (-4.5%) into a compression, a long and unpredictable stop for casual players. 4) The overall sequence (climb one side, twist down off the ridge, long descent, slow left onto the pit straight) faintly echoes Mount Panorama. The outline is clearly different, but avoid Bathurst-style naming or marketing. 5) The grid straight is only 210 m, 30 m above the 180 m rule. 6) The Switchback is a constant R30, so its exit is slow, which weakens the 490 m run to T1. 7) Party-pace lap about 1:37.7 on my model (the designer's own estimate is about 1:42 with a 15% margin), slightly under the 1:40 target. 8) Woodcutter (30 degrees, R110) is almost flat, so 'the esses' amount to one real corner.

result.winner: Kestrel Ridge (candidate d), 52/60. It has the most original silhouette and signature corner (the 205-degree descending Kestrel spiral), a clean 9-corner rhythm with spirals throughout, three evenly spaced overtaking zones after 311-490 m straights, and the largest elevation range. Ideas worth grafting in: 1) From Timberfall (a), give the Switchback an opening radius (about R30 opening to R60, like the Lantern) so it slingshots onto the main straight and the T1 slipstream; widen the T1, Hollow and Switchback braking zones to 14 m. 2) From Kettle Hollow (c), raise the Kestrel bank to about 0.09-0.10 rad and widen it to 13-13.5 m so it is a genuine two-line, side-by-side corner; add a flat-out R300 flick over the Ridge straight (Ranger's flick). 3) From Owlwood (b), add a flat 10-15 degree compression kink over a brook partway down the 470 m Fernside descent so it is not dead straight; back the exit kerbs with gravel on slow corners. Also lengthen the grid straight toward about 230 m for margin over the 180 m rule. These changes should keep D passing the checker, but they have not been run through it.

scores.name: Kestrel Ridge (d)
scores.bestIdeas:
I re-ran the checker: FAILS is empty, 3313.1 m, closure 0.0, minimum radius 30, steepest grade 6.12%, elevation range 28 m, closest legs 125 m apart, 210 m of straight behind the line. On my own speed model (1.15 g cornering, 230 km/h cap) the lap is 82.3 s; on a softer car it is 89.0 s.
- Four real braking zones, each after a long run: T1 Millrace (490 m run, 219 to 79 km/h), the Hollow (470 m run downhill, 229 to 86), the Switchback (311 m run uphill, 193 to 67) and the Kestrel (250 m ridge straight, 228 to 92).

- Best scenery of the four: the 6% Ladder climb from the brook up to a blind Brow into a fast R180 left, a ridge-top straight with views over the valley, a 205-degree spiral down around a summit knoll that you can see coming from the ridge, and a valley-floor compression at the Hollow.
- Original: the hooked '?' shape with a spiral lobe hanging off one end is unlike any Speed Dreams track. Its distance to Corkscrew is 0.171 (far) and to g-track-2 0.077, around the 28th percentile of pairs of unrelated Speed Dreams tracks.
- Clean data: width steps never exceed 1 m, banking is continuous, gravel sits outside every slow corner, and paved aprons appear only at the start straight.
- Worth reusing elsewhere: geom.py (the speed model) and preview.py.
scores.problems:
- The Kestrel shrinks from R130 to R55 over 140 degrees while going downhill at 5.4%, with about 300 m of braking while turning. That is the hardest steering job on any of the four for a phone drag, and casual players will run wide.
  - Fix: end the tightening at R65-70 and raise the bank from 0.06 to about 0.08-0.10, which makes it more like candidate c's Kettle, or open the exit sooner.
- Braking downhill into the Hollow from about 229 km/h is less forgiving for touch players.
- The Talon flick has no exit kerb (minor).
- The elevation range is 28 m against a 30 m cap, which leaves little headroom if trackgen smoothing shifts it.
- The footprint is tall and narrow (579 x 1036 m).
- Some concepts echo real circuits without matching their shape: climb one leg, wind across the top and descend the other (Bathurst), and counter-clockwise with a crest then a descending left at the top and a left hairpin onto the main straight (Laguna Seca).

scores.name: Kettle Hollow (c)
scores.bestIdeas:
I re-ran the checker: FAILS is empty, 3310.6 m, minimum radius 30, steepest grade 7.27%, elevation range 26 m, closest legs 113.7 m apart, 250 m of straight behind the line. On my speed model the lap is 81.3 s (87.9 s on a softer car).

Brands Hatch Indy: drive Kestrel Pines backwards and its corners line up one for one, in the same order and turning the same way, with Brands' seven named corners:
- T1 Millrace (105 deg) = Paddock Hill Bend
- grid and main straight = Hailwood Hill
- Switchback (163 deg) = Druids
- back straight into the Hollow (102 deg) = the short run to Graham Hill Bend
- Hollow straight, Beck bridge and Fernside dive = Cooper Straight and Surtees
- the Drop and Talon = McLaren
- Kestrel (204 deg) = Clearways and Clark Curve
- Ladder and ridge = Brabham Straight
Plotted against each other, the two heading profiles almost overlap (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-game-gang/8e5cf0a2-6c34-58a5-b66f-d0d21f7d6bf9/scratchpad/verify/out/turn_brands.png). The outline is the same type: a crescent with a hairpin finger at one end and a lobe at the other (pair_brands_indy.png, rot_brands_180.png and calib_pairs.png in the same verify/out folder; Brands Indy's corner names come from oversteer48.com/brands-hatch-indy-circuit and btcc.net/circuit/brands-hatch-indy).

What differs: the Switchback finger is a wide V (the Hollow sits about 150 m from the grid straight) rather than Druids' narrow, parallel-sided finger. Kestrel is a tight spiral, not the bulbous Clearways. The outline is straight-edged, with esses on the long east side. The lap is 1.75 times as long. It is rotated about 90 degrees from the standard Brands map and driven the other way. And T1 is flat, with nothing like Paddock's plunge.

Judgement: recognisability is borderline. The match is family-level, about as close as g-track-1 is to Knockhill, not a tracing. But Brands Indy is an iconic shape that racing-game players drive in Forza, Gran Turismo, ACC and iRacing, and someone who knows it could plausibly see "Brands Indy backwards" in the minimap. Under the default-to-true rule I am setting resemblesRealCircuit=true. Note that the design team's own shapecmp only compared against Speed Dreams tracks, so this match was never checked.
